question: Which of the following festivals of Odisha State commemorates the rich maritime history of Odisha that is celebrated throughout the state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bali Yatra**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bali Yatra is a festival that commemorates the rich maritime history of Odisha and is celebrated throughout the state.

 
 
• In the historic city of Cuttack, a week-long event is organised starting from the day of Kartika Purnima 

 
 
• (full moon day in the month of Kartik i.e October-November).
 
 
 
 
 
• Cuttack is also the commercial capital of Odisha which hosts a large number of trading and business houses in and around the city.
 
 
• It is also famous for its Durga puja which is the most important festival in Odisha and West Bengal.
 
• Cuttack is also the birthplace of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhath Puja**

 
 
• Chhath Puja is dedicated to **Surya Dev** (the Sun God) and **Chhathi Maiya** (the goddess of energy).
 
• The festival is celebrated over four days, with rituals including fasting, taking holy baths, and making offerings of **thekua** (a traditional sweet), fruits, and kheer (rice pudding) to the Sun during sunrise and sunset
 
• It involves offering prayers to the Sun for health, prosperity, and the well-being of family members.
 
 
 
• **Rath Yatra**
 
 
• Rath Yatra, primarily celebrated in Puri, Odisha, marks the annual journey of Lord Jagannath,
 
 
• along with his siblings, Balabhadra and Subhadra, in a grand chariot procession.
 
 
 
• The chariots are pulled by thousands of devotees.
 
• This festival symbolizes the unity of people from different backgrounds and communities as they come together to pull the chariots and participate in the celebrations, showcasing devotion and camaraderie.
 
 
 
• Amla Navami
 
 
• Amla Navami is a Hindu festival that celebrates the Indian gooseberry (amla), which is considered sacred and believed to have numerous health benefits.
 
• The festival typically falls on the **Navami** (ninth day) of the **Shukla Paksha** (waxing phase of the moon) in the month of **Kartika**.
